title: Input fields don't save
content:
I'm using Clo3D 2025.2.256 and since this latest update, anything I type in input fields (like Name of a pattern piece) doesn't get saved. 

Steps to reproduce:

  1. Select a pattern piece

  2. Type anything like "Test" in the Name field of the pattern piece.

  3. Select another pattern piece

  4. Select the first pattern piece again.




Problem:

The entered name is not saved. Instead, the default/previous value is there again.

The same thing also happens in nearly all the input fields in the Print Layout "Nest Settings".

### Community Post Comments:
Comment 1: Hi bettina, the name field in the Print Layout is coming from the Fabric, not the pattern itself. I have also tried importing a PDF and changing the names, and it works for me as well. If the issue is still recurring for you, please contact our support team (https://connect.clo-set.com/community/post/7f64c10b03664d5288f8d8c6c13a5c52 and share as much information as possible (files, screenshots, video recording).

Comment 2: Hi there,Did you change the name of the pattern piece in the Property Editor? I've checked on my side and I didn't manage to recreate this issue whether it's with an imported pattern piece or a newly created one.
Reply 1: Hello, yes, that's exactly the field I'm talking about. I generally work with imported pattern pieces (via PDF import). Could you please also try going into the print layout and changing the width of a fabric there using the cm or mm input fields? That's where mine is broken most consistently.
content_description: This page aims to report and troubleshoot a bug in Clo3D 2025.2.256 where input field entries, such as pattern piece names and Print Layout settings, fail to save after switching selections.

title: Topstitches issues never fixed in CLO3D
content:
So this post is about a couple issues with topstitches and bugs that I've always faced in CLO3D despite the new versions that came out.   
  
1) Topstitch tool:   
the topstitch tool seem to work fine except for one thing, the 3D toggle that activates the normal map for the topstitches is still buggy in the 3D viewport, it doesn't matter if I'm running the simulation at higher quality or not, the normal map for the **3D effect** sometimes is visible, sometimes disappears and is not visible anymore. Also the intensity slider even if you put it at 100 is not enough.   
  
2) Livesync issues:   
When using livesync 2.0 with Unreal Engine 5.6+ the imported garment gets imported with **white solid lines** when toggling "**include seampuckering normalmap** " in livesync and sometimes the UV are totally **misaligned**.   
The **white lines** correspond to the exact seam of the garment where the topstitch is _applied_. Its like a texture problem for the topstiches.  
If you**don't** toggle the "**include seampuckering normalmap** " the garment gets imported with the correct topstitches textures but no normalmap so they are very flat and badlooking, also if you have a **double needle topstitching** the second line won't be visible in UE5.6.   
If you instead just toggle "**Unified UV coordinates** " you just get horrible warped and very deep topstitching with no textures, just warped normalmaps.  
  
**__Right now is a mess to get both normalmap and good toptstitches textures in UE5.__**  
  
Also I want to point out that the imported garments in UE5 90% of the times have different material properties (but i guess that's how it works between different 3D softwares) but still, it would be nice to have a better materials compatibility without always ending up fixing the whole textures in UE5.

### Community Post Comments:
Comment 1: Hi There. It looks like there is no Active CLO subscription under this account. We always recommend posting from the account that is attached to your active CLO Subscription,For further assistance please let us know what your active CLO ID is or repost from the account with an active license. This will help us further assist youThank you
content_description: This page discusses persistent issues and bugs with CLO3D's topstitch tool and Livesync integration for Unreal Engine 5, highlighting challenges in achieving accurate 3D topstitch effects and material compatibility.

title: Happy new year in 2026
content:
## Happy new year in 2026

* * *

![b621e6113da34940bb4dec8838f63ac5](https://storagefiles.clo-set.com/public/community/202512/9f6e7a243f4740e68d57ac6181e8183e/images/b621e6113da34940bb4dec8838f63ac5Generated%20Image%20December%2026%2C%202025%20-%208_41PM.jpeg)

Hello.  
  
There are many people from different nationalities here, so I don't know how you'll greet the new year  
  
In Korea, 12 gods are given the symbol every year with 12 animals, including rats, cows, tigers, rabbits, dragons, snakes, horses, sheep, monkeys, chickens, dogs, and pigs.  
  
This year is the Year of the Red Horse, and we designed hanbok, a traditional Korean costume.  
  
You all worked hard in 2025, and I hope you have more happy things in 2026.
